newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. envoy says Colombian gov't puts him at risk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy says Colombian gov't puts him at risk.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette, branded a "sick gringo" by Colombia's interior minister, said on Monday that verbal mud-slinging and anti- American rhetoric endangered his personal security.
"The comments that have been made about me in the last few days put me in danger," Frechette said at a news conference.

"The government has the responsibility of protecting diplomats," he added, saying he hoped Colombian authorities would also look out for the safety of thousands of ordinary U.S. citizens living and working in Colombia.

U.S. embassy officials could not be reached for immediate comment on whether Frechette, an outspoken diplomat with a reputation for meddling in Colombia's internal affairs, had received any specific threat to his personal safety.

Frechette spoke after a ceremony in which he handed over $22 million in counternarcotics assistance to Colombia's National Police -- aid that has been earmarked specifically for a joint U.S.-Colombia drug crop eradication programme.

The programme, involving the aerial spraying of coca and opium poppy crops with herbicide, was suspended by Colombia last week, in apparent reprisal for Washington's decision to "decertify" the country for a second year as an ally in the drug war. The programme is to resume on Wednesday, however.

Interior Minister Horacio Serpa called Frechette a "sick gringo" in a speech on Saturday. Earlier last week a Colombian congressman called Frechette a "son-of-a-bitch" and labour leaders burned U.S. flags outside the U.S. embassy.

The protests were triggered not only by the U.S. decertification process, but by Frechette's claim, in interviews with the local news media, that two leading drug lords had repeatedly offered him evidence of President Ernesto Samper's alleged ties to the narcotics trade.
The claim prompted Samper, in a speech in the Caribbean port of Cartagena on Friday, to brand Frechette "a recycler of his own garbage."
